RAJYA SABHA 
Monday, the 25th July, 2005/3 Sravana, 1927 (Saka) 
The House met at eleven of the clock, MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair 
(The National Anthem, "Jana Gana Mana", was played) 
OBITUARY   REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri Shyam Lal, a former Member of this House; Shri Sunil 
Dutt, a sitting Member of Lok Sabha and Union Minister of Youth Affairs and 
Sports; Shri Sunder Singh Bhandari, Shri Bipinpal Das, Shri Bal Ram Singh 
Yadava and Dr. Rafiq Zakaria, former Members and Dr. Biplab Dasgupta,  a 
sitting Member of this House. 
Shri Shyam Lal, passed away on the 14 th March, 2005, at the age of 
66 years. Born at village Kusumhi in Jau npur district of Uttar Pradesh in July, 
1939. Shri Shyam Lai had his educ ation at SGRI College, Jaunpur and 
Railway Technical Institute, Lucknow. A political and social worker, Shri Shyam 
Lal was associated with various social we lfare and educational institutions. He 
was President of the Akhil Bharatiya Sh oshit Kalyan Parishad. Shri Shyam Lal 
also had a few publications to his credit. The legislative career of Shri Shyam 
Lal started with the membership of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council, 
where he was a member from May, 1984 to May, 1990. 
Shri Shyam Lal represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House from 
February, 2001 to November, 2002. In the passing away of Shri Shyam Lai, 
the country has lost a noted social worker. 
Shri Sunil Dutt passed away on the 25th May, 2005 at the age of 76 years. 
Born at Khurd village of Jhelum district  now in Pakistan, in June, 1929, Shri 
Dutt had his education at Jai Hind College, Mumbai. 
A multifaceted personality, Shri Dutt was a film artist and political and 
social worker. Shri Dutt acted in nearly 100 films and also directed and 
produced a few films. Many of his film s were screened at several International 
Film Festivals. Shri Dutt was also asso ciated with various social welfare and 
cultural organizations. 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [25 July, 2005] 
Shri Dutt was devoted to serve the cancer patients. He made a film on 
cancer and its cure and donated the profit  earned through this film to the Tata 
Memorial Hospital. He established the Nargis Dutt Memorial Foundation in 
U.S.A., U.K., Canada, Germany and Ho lland and helped different charitable 
hospitals in the country devoted to the tr eatment of cancer by ensuring supply 
of equipment worth three million US Dollars. 
Shri Dutt actively involved himself in raising funds for relief and 
rehabilitation of victims of natural calamities and communal violence. He 
himself also used to contribute generously for national and social causes. Shri 
Dutt cared for the welfare of slum dwellers and fought for providing basic 
amenities to the people living in  slums. He undertook many padyatras for 
promoting peace and communal harmony. He also organized a few 
international conferences on drug abus e and visited different parts of the 
country to promote awareness on HIV/AIDS. 
The long and illustrious political career of Shri-Dutt commenced when 
he was first elected to the Eighth Lok Sabha. He was also elected to the Ninth, 
Tenth, Thirteenth and Fourte enth Lok Sabha. He served as the Union Minister 
of Youth Affairs and Sports from May, 2004 till his sad demise. Shri Dutt also 
had the distinction of serving as Sheriff of Mumbai from 1981 to 1982. 
A recipient of Padmashree Award in 1968, Shri Dutt received several 
awards in recognition of his valuable contributions in the field of cancer 
treatment, promoting peace and communal harmony, fight against violence and 
terrorism and service to the film industry. 
Shri Sunil Dutt always stood for probity in public life. He has left 
behind an indelible mark because of his deep humanism and fight for 
communal harmony and social cohesion. I can never forget the moment when 
along with heart-rending news of his s ad demise, I received a letter from him 
which he had written just a day before his death. In response to the media 
reporting about my humble contribution for the marriage of the daughter of a 
widow of a person whose husband had donated all his organs before his death, 
Shri Dutt had enclosed with his letter a cheque of Rs. 25,ooo/-. Even this last 
act of his was one of sublime kindness; indeed throughout his life he was 
dedicated to the service of the needy and the poor. 
In the passing away of Shri Sunil Dutt, the country has lost an eminent 
parliamentarian, a brilliant actor and a great humanist. 
2 

[25 Juiy, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Shri Sunder Singh Bhandari passed away on the 22 June, 2005. at 
the age of 85 years. Born at Udaipu r in Rajasthan, Shri Bhandari had his 
education at Sirohi, Udaipur and Kanpur. 
An advocate and a teacher by profession, Shri Bhandari was an 
active social and political worker. He was one of the founder members of the 
Bharatiya Janata Party and the erstwhile Bharatiya Jana Sangh. Shri Bhandari 
served as General Secretary of the B haratiya Jana Sangh, Rajasthan, from 
1951 to 1964 and as its All India General Secretary from 1967 to 1977. He was 
also a senior Vice-President of the Bharatiya Janata Party. Shri Bhandari 
represented the State of Rajasthan in this House for two terms from April, 1966 
to April, 1972 and again from July, 1992 to April, 1998. He also represented 
the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House from April, 1976 to April, 1982. He was 
Chairman of the Committee on Petitions from 1992 to 1994 and of the 
Standing Committee on Transport and Tourism from 1996 to 1997. Shri 
Bhandari was also a member of the Indian Delegation to the Inter 
Parliamentary Union Meeting at Lisbon , Portugal in the year 1978. Shri 
Bhandari also had the distinction of servi ng as Governor of t he States of Bihar 
and Gujarat. The passing away of Shri Sunder Singh Bhandari, the country has 
lost an eminent parliamentarian and an able administrator. 
Shri Bipinpal Das passed away on the 3 rd July, 2005, at the age of 82 
years. 
Born at Guwanati in February, 1923,  Shri Das had his education at 
Cotton College, Guwahati, Presidenc y College, Kolkata and the Banaras 
Hindu University. 
An educationist, Shri Das took part in the .freedom struggle in 1942 
and courted imprisonment. He was also actively associated with various 
struggles of the people of Manipur in la te forties and early fifties and visited 
Nagaland as a member of the goodwill mission during the period of political 
unrest there in 1953. 
Having specialization in Pure Physi cs, Shri Das started his career as 
a lecturer of Physics in the Ashutosh Coll ege, Kolkata in 1945. He was also a- 
lecturer in the Darrang College of Tezpur from 1947 to 1950 and served as 
Principal and Frofessor of that college from 1959 to 1968. 
Shri Bipinpal Das represented the State of Assam in this House for 
two consecutive terms from    April, 1970 to April, 1976 and again from April, 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [25 July, 2005]  
1976 to April, 1982. He was Chief Whip of the Congress Party in Rajya Sabha 
from 1977 to 1979. He was also Chairman of the Committee on Petitions, 
Rajya Sabha from 1979 to 1982. Shri Das was also elected to the Eighth Lok 
Sabha. Shri Das served as Union Deputy Mi nister in the Ministry of External 
Affairs from 1974 to 1977. 
A widely travelled person, Shri Das was member of various Indian 
delegations and goodwill missions to abr oad and represented the country in 
several international events. He was a me mber of the Indian delegation to the 
United Nations General Assembly Session in 1971 and again attended 30 th 
Session of the U.N. in the year 1975. 
In the passing away of Shri Bipinpal Das, the country has lost a 
distinguished parliamentarian, a noted educationist and an able administrator. 
Shri Bal Ram Singh Yadava passed away on the 4th July, 2005 at the 
age of 67 years under tragic cirumstanc es. Born at village Kharagpur Sarraiya 
in Etawah District of Uttar Pradesh in April, 1939, Shri Yadava had his 
education at Etawah and Lucknow. An  advocate and an agriculturist by 
profession, Shri Yadava was an active social and political worker. He was 
keenly associated with the welfare and uplift of weaker and vulnerable sections 
of the society. He was associated with various welfare organizations and also 
stood for development of the rural areas. He was Chairman of the Uttar 
Pradesh Mandi Parishad and Uttar Pradesh Agro Industrial Corporation Limited 
from 1980 to 1982. He also served as Senior Deputy Chairman of the Uttar 
Pradesh Youth Welfare Board. 
The long and distinguished political ca reer of Shri Yadava started with 
the membership of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly from 1969 to 1974 
and again from 1980 to 1984. He served as Deputy Minister in the Government 
of Uttar Pradesh from 1969 to 1970 and as Cabinet Minister from 1971 to 1973 
and again from 1980 to 1984. Shri Yadava represented the State of Uttar 
Pradesh in this House from April, 1990 to  April, 1996. He was also elected to 
the Eighth, Twelfth and Thirteenth Lok Sabha. Shri Yadava also served as 
Union Minister of State of the Ministry of Mines from 1991 to 1995 and of the 
Ministry of Planning and Programme Implementation from 1995 to 1996. A 
widely travelled person, Shri Yadava wa s member of the Indian Parliamentary 
Delegation to Yugoslavia in the year 1986 and to Turkey in the years 1992 and 
1998. 
In the passing away of Shri Bal Ram Singh Yadava, the country has 
lost a distinguished parliamentarian and a devoted social worker. 
4 

[25 July, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Dr. Rafiq Zakaria, a former Member of this House, passed away on 
9lh July, 2005 at the age of 86 years.' Born at Sopara in Thane District of 
Maharashtra in April, 1920, Dr. Zaka ria had his education at the Bombay 
University, London University and Inns of Court, London. A Chancellor's Gold 
Medalist of the University of Bombay, Dr. Zakaria received his Ph.D. from the 
University of London. He was also called to the Bar from Lincoln's Inn. A 
lawyer and a journalist, Dr. Zakaria was associated with various social welfare 
and educational institutions in various capacities. He was Chancellor of the 
Jamia Urdu, Aligarh and helped in setting up of several educational institutions 
in Maharashtra. He was founder President of the Maulana Azad Educational 
Trust that manages various educationa l institutions at Aurangabad in 
Maharashtra. 
An outstanding scholar and historian, Dr. Zakaria was a prolific writer 
on Indian Affairs, Islam and British Imperialism. He had several publications to 
his credit. The legislative career of Dr. Zakaria, which spanned over two 
decades, started with the membership of  Maharashtra Legislative Council from 
i960 to 1962. Thereafter, he was elected to the Maharashtra Legislative 
Assembly in 1962 and remained a member of that Assembly till 1978. He 
served as Deputy Minister in the Gove rnment of Maharashtra from 1962 to 
1964 and as Cabinet Minister from 196 4 to 1977 and held the portfolios of 
Revenue, Public Health, Urban Development, Tourism and Protocol. Dr. 
Zakaria represented the State of Maharashtra in this House from April, 1978 to 
April, 1984. He was also nominated to  the Panel of Vice-Chairmen of Rajya 
Sabha for the years 1980-81, 1981-82 an d 1982-83. Dr. Zakaria represented 
India at the United Nations General Assembly. He also led the Family Planning 
Delegation of the Government of India to  the United States of America in the 
year 1969. He was special invitee to t he World of Islam Festival in London in 
the year 1976. In the passing away of Dr. Rafiq Zakaria, the country has lost 
an able parliamentarian, an eminent schol ar of Islamic history and a prolific 
writer. 
Dr. Biplab Dasgupta passed away on the 17th July, 2005 at the age of 
67 years following prolonged illness. 
Born at Kolkata in December, 1938,  Shri Dasgupta had his education 
at College of Arts and College of Law, University of Kolkata, London School of 
Economics and Institute of Computer Science, University of London. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [25 July, 2005]  
An Economist, Dr. Dasgupta started his professional career as a 
lecturer in Statistics in the Goldsmith' s College of the University of London, 
from 1965 to 1966; lecturer in Econom ics and Statistics in the University 
School of Oriental and African Studies , London, from 1966 to 1972; Reader 
and Fellow in Economics and Statistics in the Institute of Development Studies 
of the University of Sussex, from 19 72 to 1980; and was also Professor of 
Economics,   University  of    Kolkata    from    1980  to 1998. 
He was President of the Governing Body of the South Calcutta Law 
College, Kolkata since 1984 and Director of the Centre for Urban Economic 
Studies, University of Kolkata, from 1980 to 1987 and again from 1992 to 1998. 
He also held temporary assignments as Consultant and Expert with 
the United Nations for varying time periods at its various organizations namely, 
FAO, ILO, UNRISD, UNEP and UNESCO. 
Dr. Dasgupta was Convener of the U.K. Committee for Civil Liberties 
in India from 1975 to 1977. He was also Chairman of the Committee on 
Perspective Plan for Calcutta, Calcutta Metropolitan Development Authority 
and Committee on Animal Husbandry, Government of West Bengal from 1985 
to 1987. 
A prolific writer, Dr. Dasgupta had several publications to his credit. 
He was also editor of the Bengali literary monthly 'Nandan'. 
Dr. Dasgupta represented the State of  West Bengal in this House for 
two consecutive terms from April, 1994 to April, 2000 and again from April, 
2000 till he breathed his last. Dr. Das gupta was Deputy Leader of C.P.I.(M) 
Party, in Rajya Sabha from 1994 to 2004. He was also elected to the Ninth Lok 
Sabha in the year 1989. Dr. Dasgupta contributed significantly towards the 
proceedings of the House especially relating to economic and financial matters. 
Dr. Dasgupta attended many internat ional seminars, conferences and 
workshops. He was member of the ILO Employment Mission to Afghanistan in 
the year 1978. 
In the passing away of Dr. Dasgupta the country has lost an eminent 
economist, and a distinguished parliamentarian. 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Shyam Lai, Shri Sunil 
Dutt, Shri Sunder Singh Bhandari,   Shri Bipinpal Das, Shri Bal Ram Singh 
6

departed.

CHAIRMAN: Secretary-General will convey to the members of the bereaved 
families our deep sense of sorrow and sympathy. 
REFERENCES BY THE CHAIR 
Reference to victims  of bomb blasts in London 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, we in India were shocked and 
deeply saddened when we learnt of the terrorist bomb blasts in London on the 
7th of July, 2005, which resulted in the loss of so many innocent lives and 
injury to many more. We condemn the terrorist acts and express our sympathy 
and solidarity with the people of the UK in their hour of grief. 
India having been a victim of terrorism for more than two decades, 
shares with deep empathy, the anguish and pain of the people of the UK at 
these heinous acts. Such terrorist attacks underline the fact that open and 
democratic societies like our own are especially vulnerable and, therefore, 
need to strengthen cooperation, in a coordinated and concerted manner in 
order to free the world of this scourge. 
Reference to terrorist attack In Sharm-el-Sheikh, Egypt 
MR. CHAIRMAN: We are deeply shocked, appalled and grieved by 
the horrendous terrorist a ttacks on civilians in Sha rm-el-Sheikh, Egypt in the 
early hours of Friday, the 23 rd of July, 2005 on the auspicious occasion of the 
National Day of the Arab Republic of Egypt, resulting in large scale civilian 
deaths and injury. 
The Indian Parliament strongly condemns this ruthless attack on 
innocent civilians by terrorists and offers its sincere condolences to the 
bereaved families, and to the Government of the Arab Republic of Egypt. 
Terrorism which threatens peace and dialogue cannot be justified under any 
guise or motivation. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a 
mark of respect to the memory of those who lost their lives in these tragedies. 
7
